id: title:benjackwhite:strip non latin1 chars in sanitizeheadervalue

review.posthog_relevance: Protects PostHog MCP server outbound HTTP requests from ByteString conversion errors caused by non-ASCII characters in client-supplied headers.
review.reason: Adds a regex replacement to strip control characters and non-Latin-1 codepoints from HTTP header values before outbound requests, preventing potential TypeError failures in the fetch implementation.
review.uncertainty: While the implementation and its immediate relevance to PostHog's MCP server are demonstrated, the actual prevention of production incidents or false-positive alerts is not independently verified; this score reflects the bounded, substantive implementation and its plausible operational benefit rather than unobserved outcomes.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains two hunks. P1.F1.H1 is a complete, reviewable code change. P1.F2.H1 is a test file; while it adds assertions, it does not demonstrate the implementation of the new sanitization behavior, only its expected results. Therefore, this chunk cannot be treated as a single, complete implementation group. P1.F1.H1 is assessed. P1.F2.H1 is excluded from scoring.

observations.behavior: Adds a regex character class `[\x00-\x1f|[^\x00-\xff]` to the replacement string, removing not only control characters but also any codepoint outside the Latin-1 range (0x00–0xFF).
